title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Microsoft shipped Advertising MCP product news TODAY — the ad-platform MCP layer this report called table stakes on 06-29 now has a fifth member with named agency proof
bullets.summary: Microsoft Advertising published its August 2026 product post on Aug 27 leading with the Model Context Protocol server, which securely connects live Microsoft Advertising data to AI assistants including Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT and Claude, letting an agent run reports, campaign audits and keyword research in natural language without leaving the assistant. The server exposes campaigns, ad groups, ads and keywords with per-entity performance metrics — spend, clicks, impressions, CTR, average CPC, average CPM, conversions, conversion rate, revenue and ROAS — filterable and sortable, which is what makes queries like 'identify keywords with spend but no conversions in the last 30 days' a single call rather than an export. The official server was announced June 17, 2026 as an open pilot scoped to read-only reporting and audits, and it is free to connect. Two named customer results are attached rather than implied: Stagwell Media Platform combined M365 Copilot, the Advertising MCP and Azure AI Foundry to cut campaign-audit timelines from hours to minutes, and Conversios built a Performance Max audit dashboard on the server evaluating campaign health across more than 120 accounts with zero lift from its core engineering team.
bullets.how: YES, and it closes a loop this corpus opened on its very first scan. The 06-29 bullet 1 logged TikTok becoming the last of Google, Meta and Amazon to expose an MCP ads layer, and concluded that agentic campaign ops was becoming table stakes rather than an edge, with the Construct move being to wrap all four platform MCPs behind one operator agent. 'Microsoft Advertising' returns ZERO matches across all 58 corpus files, so the fifth platform has been sitting outside the thread the whole time — and it is the one most relevant to a Florida signage shop, because Bing/Microsoft search share skews older, desktop and commercial-intent, which is closer to a facilities manager sourcing monument signs than TikTok is. Three concrete reads. First, the read-only scope is a feature, not a limitation, for how Bobby actually works: an agent that audits and reports but cannot change a bid is exactly the risk profile that lets a scheduled loop run unattended, which is the same argument this report has been making about the Hermes permission boundary all week. Second, the metric surface is the useful part — spend, conversions and ROAS per keyword, queryable — because that is the missing right-hand side of the creative-abrasion loop, which currently mines GSC and GA4 for organic deltas and has no paid-side equivalent. 'Keywords with spend and no conversions' is a build target in the same shape the abrasion loop already produces. Third, the honest caveat: this is a product-news post, the pilot is read-only, and Brand 9's Microsoft Ads spend may be zero today — in which case the item is a capability to hold, not a task, and the value is knowing the surface exists before the decision to spend is made rather than after.

bullets.title: CORPUS GAP — Claude Code shipped /design ten days ago: editable UI artboards in the CLI, built on artifacts, and this report never logged it
bullets.summary: Anthropic's Week 34 digest (August 17-21, v2.1.234-v2.1.239) leads with /design, a research preview bringing Claude Design's artboard workflow into the Claude Code CLI and Claude Code Desktop. Run '/design a few options for {feature}' and Claude drafts several editable artboards for the UI, you pick one, refine it, and Claude implements it. It runs on top of artifacts — the interactive pages Claude Code publishes to claude.ai — so the drafts are shareable links rather than local files, and Claude reads the existing codebase and matches the current UI style, treating the project's design system as taking priority over its own choices. Available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. Three smaller Week 34 items shipped alongside and are also absent from this corpus: a built-in Concise output style that makes Claude lead with the result and skip preamble; a device card on your phone for any machine running 'claude remote-control', so a session can be started on that machine from the Code tab; and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL, which sets the model new sessions start on.
bullets.how: YES, logged as a corpus gap with the date stated plainly rather than dressed as news: this shipped Aug 17-21 and 'artboard', 'Concise output style', 'device card' and 'ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL' all return zero matches across 58 files, while 'Claude Design' appears exactly once, on 07-16. This report covered that week three separate times and walked past the headline feature of it. The applicability is real and specific. Bobby's visual work is governed by written brand systems — b9-brand-visual-system fixes tokens, fonts and three distinct live card patterns; b9-brand-palette fixes the six-colour system and forbids gold; vironbox-brand-kit carries the graphite-and-cyan Blueprint Standard with copy-paste head, header and footer blocks. A tool whose stated behaviour is to read the existing code and let the project's design system override its own defaults is aimed precisely at that situation, and the honest test is whether it actually respects a system expressed as a markdown skill rather than as code. The 'several options, pick one' shape is also the exact workflow the resort-signage-concepts skill runs by hand across a modern-to-classic spectrum. The two operational items matter more than they look: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL is a per-loop cost lever for a fleet of scheduled jobs that do not all need Opus, and it pairs directly with yesterday's per-loop /usage breakdown — that panel tells you which loop is expensive, this variable is how you make it cheaper. Caveat: /design is a research preview, so behaviour may change, and the design-system-priority claim is Anthropic's description of intent, not a result anyone here has verified against a B9 page.

bullets.title: Claude Code 2.1.246 quietly closed a CREDENTIAL LEAK — telemetry to Anthropic was carrying the API key configured for a third-party gateway — and extended the Bash permission-integrity work this report flagged yesterday
bullets.summary: Yesterday's bullet 8 covered 2.1.246 as the background-session-after-sleep fix plus 'a batch of fixes'. Reading the actual entry, three items in that batch are security or automation boundary work rather than polish. Telemetry and metrics requests to Anthropic were carrying the API key configured for a third-party gateway via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; a credential is now only sent to its own host. Bash permission checks now always require approval for malformed commands containing a dangling && or || operator — the same permission-integrity class as the 2.1.223 bypass this report logged yesterday, where the evaluated string differed from the executed one. And auto-mode tool calls that were being denied as 'temporarily unavailable' on very large sessions are fixed by scaling the safety-check deadline with prompt size. Two further entries touch unattended work directly: a subagent that stops at its maxTurns limit now returns its output marked as PARTIAL with a hint to continue it via SendMessage, instead of appearing finished; and the self-hosted runner no longer ends live sessions or exits when a work-poll response is malformed, such as an intercepting proxy returning an HTML page — it retries the poll.
bullets.how: YES, and the finding is that this report read a release note and stopped at the headline. 'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL', 'apiKeyHelper', 'telemetry', 'malformed command', 'dangling' and 'maxTurns' all return zero matches across 58 files, including in yesterday's own coverage of this exact version. The credential-scoping fix is the one to act on: any install pointed at a gateway or proxy was sending that gateway's key to Anthropic's telemetry endpoint, and the correct response is not alarm but a check — confirm whether any machine in the fleet sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, and if none does, the item costs nothing and is closed. The malformed-command approval change is the more structurally important one, because it is the second permission-integrity patch in three weeks and it lands on the same architecture: Hermes runs credentialed shell work from cron-dropped scripts with no operator reading a dialog, so every fix that narrows the gap between what the permission system evaluates and what the shell executes is load-bearing for a design that has no human backstop. Add it to the still-unresolved action carried from yesterday — confirm the fleet is past 2.1.223, audit Bash allow rules for a wildcard before the subcommand — and treat them as one version-and-config check rather than three tasks. The subagent maxTurns change deserves its own note: a subagent that hit a limit used to look finished, which in a scheduled loop means a truncated result silently becomes the answer, and 'partial' plus a SendMessage continuation is the difference between a wrong report and an incomplete one you can resume.

bullets.title: Frontier flat for the THIRTEENTH consecutive scan — and the falsification step killed a dated Claude Code feature that the vendor's own two release surfaces do not carry
bullets.summary: No frontier lab — OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek or Cohere — shipped a model or material availability change in this window. The trackers show twelve models released across August from seven providers, with GLM-5.2 Turbo from Z.AI on Aug 17 still the most recent entry; Gemini 3.7 Flash (Aug 13) and Meta's Muse Spark 1.2 (Aug 6) are both already in this corpus. One candidate was killed on verification and the kill is worth recording. A search summary asserted that on August 27 Claude Code announced it now writes its own feedback reports, with drafts queued locally in ~/.claude/feedback/drafts/ until sent. Checked against both vendor surfaces: the What's New digest ends at Week 34 with no such entry, and the full release-notes page carries no August 27 item at all — its newest entry is 2.1.246 and the only 'feedback' strings anywhere on it are /feedback and /bug opening immediately mid-response (2.1.229, Aug 13) and the phrase 'compaction feedback' in a 2.1.228 blurb. Suppressed as already carried: the agent-funding slate (HappyRobot's $150M at $1.2B and Zenity's $125M, both 08-21 and 08-25; Cognition's reported $1B-plus raise at $40B-plus, carried eleven times since 06-30) and the entire arXiv return (2603.09619, 2510.04618/ACE, 2602.05447, SmoothAgent 2607.00151, 2606.20683). The signage negative was re-checked yesterday and is carried forward today, labelled as carried.
bullets.how: MAYBE, and the value is the kill rather than the count. A search engine's own summary stated a feature, a date and a filesystem path — the three things that make a claim feel verified — and none of it survived contact with the vendor's release surfaces. That is the most dangerous shape of false item this report can produce, because it is specific enough to act on and would have entered the corpus as fact for every later scan to build on, which is exactly how the false 'no signage MCP server' claim once survived weeks here. The rule this hardens: a summary of a source is not the source, and a dated vendor feature gets confirmed against the vendor's own release notes or it does not ship. On the substance, thirteen flat scans is now two full months in which the ecosystem's news has been governance, packaging, cost accounting, permission boundaries and context scope — not capability. Every argument PRAGMA makes rests on that: if no competitor can differentiate on model access, the defensible layer is proprietary data and delivery discipline, which is what the AAIR score history, the answer-page corpus and the attribution chain are. The funding suppression is its own small signal — three of the largest agent rounds of the month were all already in this corpus, meaning the thread is now catching things early enough that re-reads return nothing new, which is what compounding looks like from the inside.

praxis_lesson: A search engine's SUMMARY of a source is not the source. This scan nearly shipped a Claude Code feature dated August 27, complete with a filesystem path for where drafts are queued — specific enough to feel verified and specific enough to act on — and it does not exist on either of the vendor's two release surfaces. Confirm a dated vendor feature against the vendor's own release notes or do not ship it, because a fabricated specific enters the corpus as a premise every later scan builds on. The mirror-image lesson landed in the same window: reading a release note down to the headline and stopping is how yesterday's bullet 8 covered 2.1.246 as 'a batch of fixes' while that batch contained a credential leak (telemetry to Anthropic carrying the API key set for a third-party gateway), the second Bash permission-integrity patch in three weeks (malformed commands with a dangling && or || now always require approval), and a change that stops a maxTurns-limited subagent from looking finished when it was truncated. All three matter specifically because Hermes runs credentialed shell work unattended, with no operator reading a dialog and no human noticing a partial result. Fold them into the single unresolved action carried from yesterday: one version-and-config check across the fleet — past 2.1.223, past 2.1.246, no wildcard before a Bash subcommand, and confirm whether any machine sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Separately, two capabilities were sitting in plain sight and unlogged: Microsoft Advertising's MCP server closes the ad-platform set this corpus opened on 06-29 and adds the paid-side half the creative-abrasion loop has never had, and /design shipped ten days ago into the exact workflow the B9 and VironBox brand systems govern by hand. Frontier flat for the thirteenth consecutive scan; the agent-funding slate and the entire arXiv return were suppressed as already carried, which is the first time a re-read of both categories produced nothing new.
